title: FS Time Domain v1
description: Fixed-step implicit time integration and time-indexed output controls.

method.description: Implicit scheme. Newmark is used by acoustic, elastic, low-frequency Biot poroelastic, and supported coupled Galerkin waves; backward Euler is used by pressure-form Darcy flow and temperature-form thermal diffusion. Gauss4 is fourth-order two-stage Gauss collocation for acoustic, elastic, their axisymmetric/coupled formulations, and low-frequency Biot with acoustic or bonded elastic coupling; its accepted state is real and its complex stage uses FGMRES. CPU execution supports Cartesian/cylindrical PML, GSLS, restart and MPI within the physics restrictions. Metal and CUDA/HIP support complex FGMRES stages on their existing execution paths; SYCL bulk histories, coupled interface actions and Cartesian PML filters are resident, including frequency-shifted interface filters. Bulk GSLS and composed GSLS/PML histories are also resident, with Cartesian 2D/3D MPI and checkpoint/restart support.

time_step.description: Fixed physical step size in seconds.

source.description: Shared physical-time signature. Acoustic volume injection loads its first derivative; acoustic scalar/monopole moments load its second derivative times compressibility. Forces and elastic moments load its value. Fresh waves start from zero state; volume injection requires an initially quiet signature. Impulsive step derivatives are unsupported.

interval.description: Output interval in seconds, measured from start.

times.description: Strictly increasing physical times in seconds within the integration interval.

output.description: Spatial wavefield and ParaView schedule; receiver traces inherit it unless trace_output is supplied. Select stride, interval or explicit times; default every step. Final output is always written. Explicit times and intervals must align with the integration grid.

mass_damping.description: Uniform mass-proportional bulk wave damping alpha in inverse seconds: M u_tt + (C_boundary + alpha M) u_t + K u = f. Applies to acoustic pressure and elastic displacement, including coupled and axisymmetric waves. Nonzero values require Newmark waves without PML; history loads use the CPU path. This is not constant-Q attenuation.

n_modes.description: Number of real angular acoustic modes. Task i solves order i-1, for tasks 1 through n_modes. Requires axisymmetric 2D acoustics and no simulation azimuthal_mode. Omit for a legacy single transient task.

trace_output.description: Optional independent receiver trace schedule with the same cadence rules as output. If omitted, traces inherit output. Does not change spatial wavefield or ParaView sampling.

f_0.description: Fitting frequency in Hz. Zero selects standard Gauss-4. Requires f_0*time_step < 0.5. The internal angle theta_0=2*pi*f_0*time_step sets the phase-fitted propagator coefficient.

point_source.description: Spatial policy for otherwise unregularized point loads. Explicit acquisition supports and footprints take precedence. Omission preserves legacy Dirac loading; the Python TransientJob API emits Gaussian defaults for Cartesian acoustic/elastic jobs.

f_max.description: Upper target frequency in Hz used with local material wavespeed to choose sigma.

amplitude_ratio.description: Untruncated Gaussian amplitude transfer at f_max; sigma=sqrt(-2 log(ratio))*c_min/(2*pi*f_max).

frequency.description: Frequency in Hz for ricker and sine functions.

width.description: Standard deviation in seconds for a gaussian function.

samples.description: Dimensionless recorded samples, preserved without normalization or filtering. Uniform clock t0 + n*dt, shifted by delay.

dt.description: Recorded sample interval in seconds; independent of the integration time_step.

t0.description: Physical time of the first recorded sample before delay, in seconds. Negative times are preserved.

timeFunction.description: Analytic or sampled scalar source multiplier. Sampled sources use cubic Hermite interpolation with centered interior slopes, zero endpoint slopes and zero outside the recorded interval. First/second derivatives differentiate that interpolant and require zero endpoint samples; the piecewise second derivative uses the right interval at interior knots and the left interval at the last sample.
